SI-4_title.answer: Nomograms of human hippocampal volume shifted by polygenic scores

DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: UK Biobank was used as the primary dataset for building HV nomograms from 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82. ADNI was used as an external application dataset for clinical evaluation with 818 subjects (225 CN, 391 MCI, 121 AD).
DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Data from a total of 39,664 subjects (18,718 female) aged 44-82 were obtained from the UKB (application number 65299)... In the UKB sample, 453 subjects were excluded for various conditions, 3497 for genetic ancestry, and 28 subjects were outliers: leaving a total of 35,686 subjects." and "For an application dataset, we used the ADNI database... A total of 1001 ADNI subjects (445 male) aged 55-95 were included... 26 subjects were excluded for genetic ancestry, and 314 based on HV quality scores: leaving 818 subjects."
DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Janahi2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Datasets, L217-L220; Results, L71

answer.ADNI: external evaluation and clinical application (testing nomograms on CN/MCI/AD subjects)

DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: UK Biobank healthy subjects were used to build HV nomograms using Gaussian process regression (GPR) and to create genetically adjusted nomograms stratified by PGS. ADNI was used to test the clinical utility of these nomograms by evaluating diagnostic group percentiles and longitudinal MCI-to-AD conversion.
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Using imaging data from 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 from the UK Biobank (UKB), we built HV nomograms using Gaussian process regression (GPR)" and "The UKB dataset was used to train the models and the ADNI dataset was used to test them."
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Janahi2022.pdf.md: Abstract, L41; Materials and methods / Gaussian process regression, L234

DC-3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.detail: The main nomogram was built using all 35,686 healthy UK Biobank subjects. For genetically adjusted nomograms, the top and bottom 30% of subjects stratified by PGS were used separately. No explicit train/validation/test split was reported; the entire healthy cohort was used for nomogram construction.
DC-3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.supporting_text: "In the UKB sample, 453 subjects were excluded for various conditions, 3497 for genetic ancestry, and 28 subjects were outliers: leaving a total of 35,686 subjects." and "we used the top and bottom 30% samples by PGS (at p-value<0.75 threshold) separately to build genetically adjusted nomograms."
DC-3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.location: Janahi2022.pdf.md: Results, L71; Materials and methods / Genetically adjusted nomograms, L245-L246

DC-4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: The study reports age range 44-82 years for the UK Biobank healthy subjects used for nomogram construction. Mean, SD, median, and IQR are not explicitly reported in the manuscript.
DC-4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: "Data from a total of 39,664 subjects (18,718 female) aged 44-82 were obtained from the UKB" and "GPR nomograms spanned the entire training dataset age range (45-82 years)"

DC-5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: The pre-exclusion UKB sample had 39,664 subjects with 18,718 females (47.2%) and 20,946 males (52.8%). However, the exact sex breakdown for the final 35,686 healthy subjects after exclusions is not explicitly reported. Nomograms were built separately for males and females.
DC-5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: "Data from a total of 39,664 subjects (18,718 female) aged 44-82 were obtained from the UKB" and "The dataset was then stratified by self-reported sex."
